outcome: No new mathematical development since 26 January 2024 was found; the problem's status remains exactly the contested, unsettled state it was in before the window (centered on whether Duan and Zhao's 2020 work fully resolves it), and a widely-surfacing 'Adelic Langlands Program' claim of resolution traces to a non-mathematical crank blog series, not a real proof.

disputes.summary: No consensus in the field on whether Haibao Duan and Xuezhi Zhao's 2020 solution of 'Schubert's problem of characteristics' fully resolves Hilbert's 15th problem. This dispute predates the window (the paper is from 2019/2020) and is unresolved as of the June 2026 Simons Foundation survey, so it carries forward unchanged rather than being a new event.

summary: Hilbert's 15th problem asks for a rigorous foundation for Schubert's enumerative calculus. Nothing found in the 26 January 2024 to present window changes this bullet. Three lines of inquiry converged on the same conclusion. (1) The June 2026 Simons Foundation survey 'Solved, Unsolved and Unsolvable: The Status of Hilbert's 23 Problems' gives problem 15 the verdict 'It's complicated,' explicitly stating there is 'no consensus in the field about whether 2020 work by Haibao Duan and Xuezhi Zhao fully resolves the question' -- i.e. the open dispute is the same pre-2020, pre-window one, restated without new developments. (2) A June 2025 arXiv handbook chapter, 'Introduction to the Cohomology of the Flag Variety' by Billey, Gao and Pawlowski (arXiv:2506.21064), is a survey/computational introduction to Schubert calculus that states in its own framing that thanks to 'many contributions in algebraic topology, geometry, and combinatorics, we consider this solved' -- referring to the cumulative 20th-century foundational work (van der Waerden, Weil, Chevalley, Ehresmann, Bernstein-Gelfand-Gelfand, etc.), not to any new 2024+ result. It is a pedagogical/computational survey, not a new resolution. (3) A claim that an 'Adelic Langlands Program' resolves Hilbert's 15th problem appears in search results (a YouTube video title and a Medium blog series), which the triage pass flagged as unsourced. I traced the Medium series ('Logos Field Theory,' by an author using the handle jhblank7497) and found it is a self-published, non-peer-reviewed, thousands-of-volumes-long personal theory mixing legitimate terms (adelic numbers, Langlands correspondence) with speculative claims about consciousness, a computational 'operating system' universe, and a 'Theory of Everything.' No arXiv paper, journal article, or expert digestion of any 'Adelic Langlands' resolution of Hilbert's 15th problem exists; targeted arXiv searches for the phrase returned nothing on-topic. This is not mathematics and not evidence of anything happening to the problem, let alone AI involvement. No AI system was found to have been used to produce any relevant mathematical result on this problem in the window (the crank blog's authorship/tools were not established and are irrelevant regardless, since its content is not a mathematical result).
competing_reading: One could argue the June 2026 Simons Foundation piece itself constitutes a 2026 'event' worth a status of some kind, since it is dated within the window. But it is explicitly a status survey of existing (2020 and earlier) work with no new mathematical content, and it reaches the same 'no consensus' conclusion that predates the window; it does not move the problem, so it is treated as evidence for 'no change found' rather than as a dated event in its own right.
what_would_settle_it: A peer-reviewed paper or widely-cited preprint published after 26 January 2024 that either (a) settles the Duan-Zhao dispute by community consensus, or (b) presents a genuinely new rigorous foundation for Schubert calculus (or a specific gap in the existing foundation) that experts engage with. Also relevant: any statement from Duan, Zhao, or recognized experts in Schubert calculus/algebraic geometry taking a new position on the 2020 work within the window.
